subject: history_social
passage: A restaurant chain asks diners to fill out comment cards voluntarily at the end of their meals. Of the cards collected last year, 70 percent contained complaints, and a manager concluded that most of the chain's customers were unhappy. Survey researchers have long found, however, that people with strong feelings, particularly negative ones, are much more likely than others to volunteer feedback. When the chain later telephoned a randomly selected group of recent diners, 85 percent said they were satisfied with their meals. Taken together, these findings suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the comment cards likely exaggerate how common dissatisfaction is among diners.
choices.B: the quality of the chain's meals improved after the comment cards were collected.
choices.C: most diners who fill out comment cards are visiting the chain for the first time.
choices.D: the telephone survey mainly reached diners who had already filled out comment cards.

explanation.why: Comment cards are voluntary, and unhappy people are especially likely to volunteer feedback, so complaints will be overrepresented on the cards. The random phone survey avoids that problem and found most diners satisfied. Together, these points suggest the cards overstate dissatisfaction.
explanation.A: Correct. Self-selected cards overrepresent strong negative feelings, and the random survey shows most diners were satisfied.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text offers no evidence that the food changed; the difference comes from who answered.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text gives no information about how often card writers had visited.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says the phone survey reached a randomly selected group, not mainly people who had complained.
